newsitem.title: PERU: Peru posts 1.7 pct Jan-Oct cumulative GDP rise.
newsitem.headline: Peru posts 1.7 pct Jan-Oct cumulative GDP rise.

text.p: The Peruvian economy grew 1.7 percent in the first ten months of the year, compared to 7.6 percent in the same period of 1995, the National Institute of Statistics and Information (INEI) said Thursday.
The INEI added that year-on-year gross domestic product (GDP) contracted 0.8 percent in October, compared with 3.1 percent year-on-year growth in the same month last year.
October was the first time the Peruvian economy showed a monthly year-on-year contraction since March, when it registered a figure of minus 1.1 percent.

The cumulative growth in the first ten months of 1996 was led by the agriculture sector, which rose 5.0 percent, followed by 3.3 percent growth in mining, 2.6 percent in the trade sector, 1.4 percent in the electricity sector and 1.2 percent for manufacturing, the INEI said.
The INEI's "others" group, which encompasses the banking, insurance, transport and government sectors, saw economic growth in the first ten months of 2.3 percent.
In contrast, the fishing sector contracted in the first ten months by 7.9 percent, while construction was off 6.1 percent in the same period, the INEI said.
The government is predicting annual growth of 2.5 percent in 1996, down from initial projections of between five and six percent due to a longer-than-expected economic slowdown.
It is aiming for five percent growth in 1997.
In 1995, the economy expanded 7.0 percent, Latin America's second-highest growth rate, down from 13.1 percent in 1994, according to revised Central Reserve Bank figures.
